description: TTS server (MODEL_SERVICE=tts) — the stages of speech generation measured separately so a slowdown can be pinned to one of them: request conditioning (built from the request text, or from a voice sample), autoregressive codec-token decode, and vocoder waveform reconstruction. Conditioning carries p50/p99 per stage and a share-of-engine-time reading, because short utterances can be dominated by preprocessing rather than by synthesis.
title: TT Media Server — TTS (decode + vocoder + conditioning)

panels.description: Fraction of total request time spent preparing the request rather than synthesizing it, summed over all stages. This is the headline: when it climbs, requests are being spent on preprocessing, which is what happens as utterances get shorter — the fixed cost of conditioning stops being amortized over enough audio. Time-weighted from the _sum series, because quantiles cannot be summed.
panels.title: Conditioning Share of Engine Time

panels.description: 99th percentile conditioning latency across the selected stages — the tail a request can pay before synthesis even starts.
panels.title: Conditioning p99

panels.description: Median conditioning latency across the selected stages. Read against p99 to see whether preprocessing cost is uniform or spiky — a wide gap usually means a cold voice-sample cache on some requests.
panels.title: Conditioning p50

panels.description: Median total request time, from service entry through the terminal event. The denominator the share above divides into, shown so a high share can be read as either slow conditioning or a very short request.
panels.title: Request Duration p50

panels.description: Per-stage tail latency. The four stages are disjoint work on two mutually exclusive paths. No voice sample: text_conditioning, in the main process, covering that path end to end — tokenizer lookup and prompt compilation both. With a voice sample: voice_normalization in the main process, then voice_encode (encoding the reference WAV into speech IDs on device) and prompt_compile in the worker, reaching here on the request's terminal IPC message. text_conditioning and prompt_compile never both run for one request, so prompt_compile is always the worker-side, post-encode compile. voice_encode is normally the largest and is absent entirely on a voice-sample cache hit.
panels.title: Conditioning p99 by Stage

panels.description: Per-stage median latency. Comparing this with the p99 panel beside it shows which stage contributes the tail rather than the typical cost.
panels.title: Conditioning p50 by Stage

panels.description: Each stage's own share of request time, stacked so the total is the headline share. This is where 'short utterances are dominated by preprocessing' becomes visible per stage rather than in aggregate.
panels.title: Share of Engine Time by Stage

panels.description: Mean seconds per observation, rate(_sum)/rate(_count). Unlike the quantiles this is safe to compare across stages and reconstructs the per-request cost that the share panel expresses as a fraction. A stage with no observations in the window simply has no line — which is how a warm voice-sample cache reads.
panels.title: Mean Conditioning per Request by Stage

panels.description: How often each stage actually runs. Reading this next to the latency panels separates 'this stage got slower' from 'this stage started running on more requests' — a voice_encode rate climbing toward the request rate means the voice-sample cache has stopped absorbing repeats.
panels.title: Conditioning Observations/s by Stage

panels.description: Acoustic/codec tokens generated per second across every device and replica in the current filter. This is the autoregressive decode capacity of the TTS model.
panels.title: Codec Tokens/s

panels.description: Highest per-device codec-token rate. A large gap between this and the per-device average means work is unevenly spread across devices.
panels.title: Busiest Device

panels.description: Total acoustic tokens emitted since the workers last (re)started. Drops to zero on a worker restart.
panels.title: Codec Tokens (cumulative)

panels.description: TTS worker processes currently running (one per DEVICE_IDS group).
panels.title: Workers Alive

panels.description: Per-device codec-token throughput. `device` is the worker's DEVICE_IDS group (its TT_VISIBLE_DEVICES value). Watch for one device falling behind the others — it caps the whole replica's concurrency.
panels.title: Codec Tokens/s by Device

panels.description: Throughput split by how the voice was specified: `default` (no prompt), `description` (free-form voice prompt) or `voice_sample` (cloned from an uploaded WAV). The TTS API exposes no voice ID or language field, so this is the finest voice granularity available today — per-voice and per-language breakdowns need those fields added to the request first.
panels.title: Codec Tokens/s by Voice Source

panels.description: Per-replica throughput. `instance` is the Prometheus scrape target — one series per server replica, summed over that replica's devices.
panels.title: Codec Tokens/s by Replica

panels.description: Full granularity in one view: codec tokens/s broken out by model, device, replica and voice source. Empty rows mean that combination produced no tokens in the window.
panels.title: Codec Tokens/s by Model / Replica / Device / Voice Source

panels.description: Seconds of audio the vocoder reconstructs per wall-clock second — the real-time factor. Below 1.0 waveform reconstruction cannot keep up with playback even if token generation can, which is the failure this row exists to catch. Above 1.0 there is headroom for concurrency.
panels.title: Audio Seconds/s (RTF)

panels.description: PCM frames (samples per channel) reconstructed per second across the current filter. The same measurement as the RTF stat before dividing by the output sample rate.
panels.title: Samples/s

panels.description: Total audio duration this deployment has reconstructed since its workers last restarted.
panels.title: Audio Emitted (cumulative)

panels.description: TTS_AUDIO_SAMPLE_RATE_HZ as published by the workers. The divisor that turns frames into audio seconds; shown so a misconfigured rate is visible rather than silently skewing every RTF number here.
panels.title: Output Sample Rate

panels.description: Per-device vocoder throughput. `device` is the worker's DEVICE_IDS group (its TT_VISIBLE_DEVICES value). A single device below the others caps the replica's usable concurrency.
panels.title: Audio Seconds/s by Device

panels.description: Vocoder throughput split by how many streams were reconstructed together. This is the panel that answers whether waveform reconstruction scales with batch: if per-sweep throughput is flat from batch 1 to batch 8, batching is buying nothing and the vocoder is the ceiling. The batch size is derived by the runner (distinct streams per drain sweep), not reported by the engine, and it errs both ways: a batch split across two sweeps appears as two smaller buckets, while two batches finishing inside the runner's 1 ms sleep are drained together and appear as one larger one. The over-count is the flattering direction — it makes reconstruction look like it scales with batch better than it does — so read a shift in the distribution rather than any single bucket.
panels.title: Audio Seconds/s by Vocode Batch

panels.description: Codec tokens generated per second divided by audio seconds reconstructed per second. The codec has a fixed token rate per second of audio, so this line is flat when both stages keep pace. It rises when the vocoder falls behind a healthy decoder, and falls when the decoder is the one starving — which is what separates a waveform-reconstruction bottleneck from a token-generation one.
panels.title: Codec Tokens per Audio Second

panels.description: Frames divided by chunks over the same interval. When audio throughput drops this tells apart 'fewer chunks' (the vocoder is running less often) from 'shorter chunks' (it is producing less per run).

targets.expr: sum by (batch) (rate(tt_tts_audio_frames_total{device=~"$device", batch=~"$batch"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (batch) (rate(tt_tts_vocoder_chunks_total{device=~"$device", batch=~"$batch"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mean Frames per Chunk by Batch

panels.description: Per-replica vocoder throughput, from the scrape `instance` label. Divergence between replicas serving the same model points at the host or its device group rather than the model.
panels.title: Audio Seconds/s by Replica

panels.description: Vocoder throughput in audio seconds per second, broken out along every dimension the series carries.

targets.expr: sum by (model_name, instance, device, batch) (rate(tt_tts_audio_frames_total{device=~"$device", batch=~"$batch"}[$__rate_interval])) / scalar(max(tt_tts_audio_sample_rate_hz))

panels.title: Audio Seconds/s by Model / Replica / Device / Batch

panels.description: Seconds since each worker last emitted a codec token. Rising while requests are in flight means the decoder has stalled — speech will fall behind playback.
panels.title: Time Since Last Codec Token

panels.description: Seconds since each worker last emitted a vocoded audio chunk. Read next to 'Time Since Last Codec Token': this one rising while that one stays flat is the vocoder stalling behind a decoder that is still producing tokens. Both rising together points upstream instead.
panels.title: Time Since Last Vocoded Chunk

panels.description: Seconds since each TTS worker last completed a scheduler step. A flat non-zero line means the worker loop is wedged.
panels.title: Worker Heartbeat Age

panels.description: 1 while the worker process is running, 0 once WorkerManager sees it exit.
panels.title: Worker Alive
